'''Tails''', or "'''The Amnesic Incognito Live System'''", is a [[Security-focused operating system|security-focused]] [[Debian]]-based [[Linux distribution]] running on a computer, aimed at preserving [[Internet privacy|privacy]] and [[anonymity]] against [[internet surveillance|surveillance]].{{r|LWN}} It connects to the [[Internet]] exclusively through the anonymity [[overlay network]] [[Tor (network)|Tor]].{{r|TC}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alternative Networks |url=https://www.privacyguides.org/en/alternative-networks/ |access-date=2025-11-12 |website=Privacy Guides |language=en}}</ref> The system is designed to be [[Booting|booted]] as a [[live DVD]] or [[live USB]] and never writes to the [[hard drive]] or [[SSD]], leaving no [[digital footprint]] on the machine unless explicitly told to do so.

In 2024, Tails merged with the [[The Tor Project|Tor Project]].<ref name="tails-merger"/><ref name="techcrunch-merger"/>

== History ==
Tails was first released on June 23, 2009. It is the next iteration of development on [[Incognito (Operating System)|Incognito]], a discontinued [[Gentoo Linux|Gentoo]]-based Linux distribution.{{r|LJ}} The original project was called Amnesia. The operating system was born when Amnesia was merged with Incognito.<ref name=wired>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.wired.com/2014/04/tails/ |title=Out in the Open: Inside the Operating System Edward Snowden Used to Evade the NSA |last=Finley |first=Klint |date=14 Apr 2014 |magazine=WIRED |access-date=18 Apr 2014 |archive-date=April 19, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140419003312/http://www.wired.com/2014/04/tails/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The Tor Project provided financial support for its development in the beginnings of the project.<ref name="finances">{{cite web|title=Finances|url=https://tails.boum.org/doc/about/finances/index.en.html|website=Tails|access-date=13 May 2013|date=4 April 2013|archive-date=March 29, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190329135508/https://tails.boum.org/doc/about/finances/index.en.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Tails also received funding from the [[Open Technology Fund]], [[Mozilla]], and the [[Freedom of the Press Foundation]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tails.boum.org/news/report_2014_05/index.en.html|title=Tails report for May, 2014|website=Tails|date=14 Jun 2014|access-date=July 6, 2014|archive-date=July 1, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140701134844/https://tails.boum.org/news/report_2014_05/index.en.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[Laura Poitras]], [[Glenn Greenwald]], [[Bruce Schneier]] and [[Barton Gellman]] have each said that Tails was an important tool they used in their work with [[National Security Agency]] whistleblower [[Edward Snowden]].<ref name=wired/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://pressfreedomfoundation.org/blog/2014/04/help-support-little-known-privacy-tool-has-been-critical-journalists-reporting-nsa |title=Help Support the Little-Known Privacy Tool That Has Been Critical to Journalists Reporting on the NSA |last=Timm |first=Trevor |date=2 Apr 2014 |website=Freedom of the Press Foundation |access-date=18 Apr 2014 |archive-date=July 20, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140720192050/https://pressfreedomfoundation.org/blog/2014/04/help-support-little-known-privacy-tool-has-been-critical-journalists-reporting-nsa |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://gizmodo.com/try-the-super-secure-usb-drive-os-that-edward-snowden-i-1563320487|title=Try the Super-Secure USB Drive OS That Edward Snowden Insists on Using|last=Condliffe|first=Jamie|date=15 Apr 2014|website=Gizmodo|access-date=15 Apr 2014|archive-date=April 15, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140415110816/http://gizmodo.com/try-the-super-secure-usb-drive-os-that-edward-snowden-i-1563320487|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Air Gaps - Schneier on Security |url=https://www.schneier.com/blog/archives/2013/10/air_gaps.html |access-date=2023-08-03 |website=www.schneier.com |date=October 11, 2013 |archive-date=August 3, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230803152512/https://www.schneier.com/blog/archives/2013/10/air_gaps.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

From release 3.0 (2017) onwards, Tails requires a [[64-bit processor]] to run.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tails - Tails 3.0 is out|url=https://tails.boum.org/news/version_3.0/index.en.html|website=tails.boum.org|access-date=14 June 2017|archive-date=May 22, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190522152235/https://tails.boum.org/news/version_3.0/index.en.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

<span data-darkreader-inline-color="" data-darkreader-inline-bgcolor="">In 2023, the </span>Tails Project <span data-darkreader-inline-color="" data-darkreader-inline-bgcolor="">approached the [[The Tor Project|Tor Project]] to merge operations. The merger was completed on September 26, 2024, stating that, "By joining forces, the Tails team can now focus on their core mission of maintaining and improving Tails OS, exploring more and complementary use cases while benefiting from the larger organizational structure of The Tor Project."</span><ref name="tails-merger">{{Cite web |title=Tails - Uniting for Internet Freedom: Tor Project & Tails Join Forces |url=https://tails.net/news/tails_tor/ |access-date=2024-09-26 |website=tails.net |archive-date=2024-09-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240926153057/https://tails.net/news/tails_tor/ |url-status=live |date=2024-09-26}}</ref><ref name="techcrunch-merger">{{Cite web |last=Sawers |first=Paul |date=2024-09-26 |title=The Tor Project merges with Tails, a Linux-based portable OS focused on privacy |url=https://techcrunch.com/2024/09/26/the-tor-project-merges-with-tails-a-linux-based-portable-os-focused-on-privacy/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240926122144/https://techcrunch.com/2024/09/26/the-tor-project-merges-with-tails-a-linux-based-portable-os-focused-on-privacy/ |archive-date=2024-09-26 |access-date=2024-09-26 |website=[[TechCrunch]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Features ==
<!-- This section is not for a comprehensive list of software. -->
Tails must be installed on a DVD or USB stick dedicated to running Tails only, for security,<ref>{{cite web |title=Frequently asked questions: Do I need a USB stick dedicated to Tails? |url=https://tails.net/support/faq/index.en.html#dedicated-stick |website=Tails |access-date=13 June 2026}}</ref> and must be run on a [[PC-compatible computer]], not a [[mobile phone]] or [[tablet computer|tablet]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Install Tails | publisher=Tails| url=https://tails.net/install/ | access-date=26 February 2026}}</ref> Though the system can also run as a [[virtual machine]], running Tails in a virtual machine is potentially insecure.<ref>{{cite web |title=Running Tails in a virtual machine |url=https://tails.net/doc/advanced_topics/virtualization/index.en.html |website=Tails |access-date=13 June 2026}}</ref>

Tails' [[Pre-installed software|pre-installed]] [[desktop environment]] is [[GNOME]]. The system includes essential software for functions such as reading and editing documents, editing images, watching videos, printing, and instant messaging.<ref name=features>{{cite web|url=https://tails.boum.org/doc/about/features/index.en.html|title=Features and included software|date=7 October 2019|website=tails.boum.org|access-date=7 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190823092502/https://tails.boum.org/doc/about/features/index.en.html|archive-date=23 August 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> It also includes specialized security software such as [[GNU Privacy Guard|GnuPG]] to [[Digital signature|sign]] and [[Encryption|encrypt]] files, the cryptocurrency wallet [[Electrum (software)|Electrum]], and [[OnionShare]] to share files anonymously. Other software from Debian can be installed at the user's behest.<ref>{{cite web |title=Installing additional software |url=https://tails.net/doc/persistent_storage/additional_software/index.en.html |website=Tails |access-date=13 June 2026}}</ref> Despite being [[Open-source software|open-source]], Tails contains non-free [[firmware]] [[Binary blob|blobs]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Explaining Why We Don't Endorse Other Systems |url=https://www.gnu.org/distros/common-distros.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622234047/https://www.gnu.org/distros/common-distros.html |archive-date=2023-06-22 |access-date=2023-06-23 |website=www.gnu.org}}</ref>

Tails forces all network connections to use [[Tor (anonymity network)|Tor]] and includes a modified version of [[Tor Browser]] that comes with the [[uBlock Origin]] browser extension.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Browsing the web with Tor Browser |url=https://tails.boum.org/doc/anonymous_internet/Tor_Browser/index.en.html#fingerprint |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220208114930/https://tails.boum.org/doc/anonymous_internet/Tor_Browser/index.en.html#expand |archive-date=2022-02-08 |access-date=2022-03-16 |website=tails.boum.org}}</ref>

By design, Tails is "amnesic". It runs in the computer's [[random access memory]] (RAM) and does not write to the [[hard drive]] or [[SSD]]. The user may choose to keep files, applications or some settings on their Tails drive in "Persistent Storage", which is [[Encryption|encrypted]] by default, but is not hidden and easily detectable, though not readable, by forensic analysis.<ref>{{cite web |title=Persistent Storage |url=https://tails.net/doc/persistent_storage/index.en.html |website=Tails |access-date=13 June 2026}}</ref> While shutting down, Tails [[Data erasure|overwrites]] most of the used RAM to avoid a [[cold boot attack]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Protection against cold boot attacks |url=https://tails.net/doc/advanced_topics/cold_boot_attacks/index.en.html |website=Tails |access-date=13 June 2026}}</ref>

== Hardware support ==
Tails is based on [[Linux]]. Linux generally supports a wide range of hardware, including many older devices, due to standardized drivers. There may be problems with some hardware for which Linux drivers are not available, or not supported by Tails. Wi-Fi hardware, in particular, can be incompatible without a workaround, requiring a cable for Internet connection. Touchpads and graphics can cause problems which can be worked around.<ref>{{cite web | title=Known issues - sections 'Networking issues' and 'Other hardware issues'| publisher=Tails | url=https://tails.net/support/known_issues/index.en.html | access-date=26 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-22 |title=The Battle for Wireless Drivers in Linux and BSD – OSnews |url=https://www.osnews.com/story/16782/the-battle-for-wireless-drivers-in-linux-and-bsd/ |access-date=2025-05-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250322094207/https://www.osnews.com/story/16782/the-battle-for-wireless-drivers-in-linux-and-bsd/ |archive-date=March 22, 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-07-28 |title=Why does Wi-Fi have to be such a pain in Linux? - LinuxQuestions.org |url=http://www.linuxquestions.org/questions/blog/ichase-534483/why-does-wi-fi-have-to-be-such-a-pain-in-linux-3443/ |access-date=2025-05-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170728113703/http://www.linuxquestions.org/questions/blog/ichase-534483/why-does-wi-fi-have-to-be-such-a-pain-in-linux-3443/ |archive-date=July 28, 2017 }}</ref>

==Security incidents==
In 2014, [[Das Erste]] reported that the US [[National Security Agency]] (NSA)'s [[XKeyscore]] surveillance system sets threat definitions for people who search for Tails using a search engine or visit the Tails website. A comment in XKeyscore's source code calls Tails "a [[communications security|comsec]] mechanism advocated by [[Extremism|extremists]] on extremist forums".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://daserste.ndr.de/panorama/aktuell/NSA-targets-the-privacy-conscious,nsa230.html |first1=J. |last1=Appelbaum |author-link1=Jacob Appelbaum |first2=A. |last2=Gibson |first3=J. |last3=Goetz |first4=V. |last4=Kabisch |first5=L. |last5=Kampf |first6=L. |last6=Ryge |title=NSA targets the privacy-conscious |website=DasErste.de |date=3 Jul 2014 |access-date=July 3, 2014 |archive-date=May 23, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160523073009/http://daserste.ndr.de/panorama/aktuell/NSA-targets-the-privacy-conscious,nsa230.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.schneier.com/blog/archives/2014/07/nsa_targets_pri.html|title=NSA Targets Privacy Conscious for Surveillance|author=[[Bruce Schneier]]|work=Schneier on Security|date=3 Jul 2014|access-date=July 3, 2014|archive-date=June 20, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230620075434/https://www.schneier.com/blog/archives/2014/07/nsa_targets_pri.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

In the same year, {{lang|de|[[Der Spiegel]]}} published slides from an internal NSA presentation dating to June 2012, in which the NSA deemed Tails on its own as a "major threat" to its mission and in conjunction with other privacy tools as "catastrophic".{{r|"spiegel1"}}{{r|"spiegel2"}}

In 2017, the US [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] (FBI) used malicious code developed by [[Facebook]], identifying sexual extortionist and Tails user [[Buster Hernandez]] through a [[zero-day vulnerability]] in the system's default video player, [[GNOME Videos]]. The exploit was never explained to or discovered by the Tails developers, but it is believed that the vulnerability was patched in a later release of Tails. Hernandez had eluded authorities for a long time; the FBI and Facebook had searched for him with no success, and resorted to developing the custom hacking tool. He was arrested in 2017, and in 2021 he was sentenced to 75 years in prison.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/facebook-helped-fbi-hack-child-predator-buster-hernandez/ |title=Facebook Helped the FBI Hack a Child Predator |newspaper=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]] |date=10 Jun 2020 |first=Lorenzo |last=Franceschi-Bicchierai |access-date=June 12, 2020 |archive-date=June 13, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200613000336/https://www.vice.com/en_us/article/v7gd9b/facebook-helped-fbi-hack-child-predator-buster-hernandez |url-status=live }}</ref>
